chunks: Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding collateral that if it was greater than the amount of the creditor’s property and it was destroyed, the excess must be paid to the owner of the collateral. And if the collateral was less than his property and the collateral was destroyed, its owner must pay him the remainder of his property. And if the collateral was equal in value to what he pledged, then nothing is due upon him.

key_terms.الرَّهْنِ: pledged collateral held against a debt
key_terms.الْفَضْلُ: the excess amount beyond the debt
key_terms.الْمُرْتَهِنِ: the creditor who holds the pledged item
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الرَّهْنِ: the owner of the pledged collateral
key_terms.مَالِهِ: the amount of property or debt owed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if pledged collateral is destroyed and its value is more, less, or equal to the debt?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling concerning rahn (pledged collateral) in relation to the amount of debt. It explains how liability is determined when the collateral is destroyed: any excess value belongs to the owner, any shortfall remains owed, and if both are equal, neither party owes anything further.
